maya: FYI: after today's merge of optimize-attn-tiling (PR #4821) canary shows decode p95 up ~2.8x on short sequences (<=16). p50 looks fine. CI perf job flagged. :eyes:

sam: Ugh. Link to perf run: https://ci.internal/perf/4821-canary — any traces or flamegraphs?

maya: Quick summary from canary host: decode_path p95 0.9ms -> 2.7ms, cpu-side scheduling stable, KV cache hit latency unchanged. Problem only shows up for shortseq workloads. No OOMs.

nik: Did the kernel selector flip to the tiled attention kernel for short sequences? That selector tweak landed in the same PR.

maya: Yes — selector logic in runtime/kernel_selector.cc now has `if (seq_len <= 32 && head_dim >= 64) use_tiled_attn = true` — looks aggressive for tiny seqs.

lee: On the canary GPU I see SM utilization up and a lot more kernel launches per request. Stack traces point at kernel launch overhead and more short post-processing kernels.

alexa: I reproduced locally with our shortseq microbench. Results: `shortseq-16: baseline old_attn 0.9ms, tiled_attn 2.5ms` — tiling moves work into multiple kernels. Pasted nvprof snippet below.

alexa: ```
# nvprof summary (shortseq-16)
kernel: tiled_attn_tile    - 1.8ms (calls: 10)
kernel: tiled_attn_post    - 0.4ms (calls: 10)
kernel: old_unfused_attn   - 0.3ms (calls: 1)
```

sam: That matches theory: tiled path splits into many small kernels; for small seq/batch the per-kernel overhead dominates.

nik: Also note the merge added a small scheduler tweak that favors tile-friendly kernels by splitting batches differently. Possible combinatorial effect: more kernel launches *and* smaller batches.

maya: Ops bot posted: "canary-autoblock: rollout paused for release/2026-03-18 due to perf delta > threshold" — so rollout is already stopped.

lee: If revert is expensive, we can push a hotfix guard: require seq_len >= 64 before choosing tiled_attn. Quick and minimal.

sam: +1 for patch guard + CI microbench. We should avoid full revert unless patch fails.

alexa: I'll open a PR with selector guard and perf unit that asserts no >1.5x p95 regression for seq<=32. Will include local bench and nvprof traces.

maya: Also run `git bisect` to be safe, but it looks correlated with PR #4821. Command I used: `git bisect start -- bad v2026-03-18 good v2026-03-17` then narrowed to 7f3a2.

nik: If we revert or change selector, remember quantized kernel path differences — tiled kernel used a different accumulation precision in the quant pipeline. Need to validate numeric parity.

lee: I'm adding a canary tracing hook to collect kernel launch counts per request and the scheduler batch sizes so we can validate the hypothesis.

sam: Plan summary: 1) Block rollout (done). 2) Patch selector guard to seq_len >= 64 (alexa PR). 3) Re-run canary + perf job. 4) If passes, promote and backfill CI microbench. 5) If fails, revert PR #4821. Longer: invest in adaptive cost model that profiles host-level kernel costs.

alexa: PR opened: https://git.internal/pr/4830 — selector guard + perf test. Kicking off canary now.

ci-bot: Perf job 4821-canary - FAILED - p95 decode increased from 0.9ms -> 2.7ms (+200%). See https://ci.internal/perf/4821-canary/details

maya: Thanks everyone. Please paste nvprof/flamegraphs into the PR and update the issue. I'll coordinate next steps depending on canary run. :thumbsup:
